faults.note: Why momentum survives is reasoned well: equal and opposite pushes, lasting the same time. Why kinetic energy can be lost is not. 'Energy has no direction, so nothing cancels it' is a slogan, not a cause. Give the squash: some movement energy goes into squashing the balls, a perfectly springy ball gives it all back, a real one turns some into heat and sound. Screen 6 repeats the slogan; replace it there too. 'Each direction keeps its own total' on a glancing hit is asserted; add that the pushes are equal and opposite, so their parts in any direction are too.

'Neither total is kept ball by ball, only for the whole set' reads as if the kinetic energy total is always kept for the set, which the sticking example just contradicted. Say the momentum total is kept for the set, and the kinetic energy total only in an elastic collision. 'A light ball comes back off a heavier one' is already scoped to a bouncy enough hit; 'Two equal balls ... swap velocities' is scoped to ideal bouncy and head-on, so it stands.
